samples.summary: Cmd+Shift+V's post-await write has no `disposed` guard, unlike every other deferred paste write. This delta's new test pins this async path as a supported one-undo-unit action, so the missing guard is now load-bearing.
samples.evidence: `pastePlainTextFromClipboard` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4242-4256) awaits `navigator.clipboard.readText()` and then, with no re-validation, calls `this.saveSnapshot()` and opens a `withUndoUnit` batch that deletes the selection and inserts text. The only other write that resumes after a yield does re-validate: `deferPaste` at packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1606-1608 — `if (!this.disposed) job();` with the comment "The host can unmount during the frame this waited for; writing through a disposed editor would mutate a document nothing renders." A user pressing Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+V and immediately navigating away (docs-view unmount → `dispose()`) resolves the clipboard promise after teardown and writes a full select-all replacement into the store through a torn-down editor. The fix belongs on the new code path in text-editor.ts (add the `disposed` check, mirroring line 1608).

samples.summary: `pastePlainTextFromClipboard` writes after its await without checking `this.pasting`, so it can land inside a large paste's yield gap that every other write path is guarded against.

The new test in this delta (packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/editor-undo-selection.test.ts:432) treats this async path as a first-class composite action, which is what makes the unguarded gap worth closing. Fix belongs in text-editor.ts's plain-paste path.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: `pastePlainTextFromClipboard` (text-editor.ts:4242-4256) is one of only two async functions in the file, and it resumes after `await navigator.clipboard.readText()` to call `saveSnapshot()` + `withUndoUnit(deleteSelection/insertPlainText)` with no lifecycle re-validation. The only `disposed` references in packages/docs/src are the field (368), the deferPaste check (1608) and `dispose()` (6053) — there is no alternately-named guard (`isDisposed`, `destroyed` absent) and no indirect one: `withUndoUnit` (3839) calls `this.doc.batch` directly, `dispose()` (6052-6078) only detaches DOM listeners without nulling `this.doc`, and `YorkieDocStore` has no disposed-write rejection, so a post-dispose write opens a real `doc.update` on the live document. The field doc at 364-366 explicitly claims the deferred paste job is "the one piece of work that can outlive the editor", an invariant this second async write violates. In-lane for blast radius (guard/invariant with a reachable bypass outside the diff) and major: a select-all replacement can land in the store through a torn-down editor.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `pastePlainTextFromClipboard` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4242-4256) awaits `navigator.clipboard.readText()` and then writes (`saveSnapshot` + `withUndoUnit(deleteSelection/insertPlainText/setRange/requestRender)`) with no post-await re-check. A grep for `pasting` across all of packages/docs/src returns only 361, 887/893, 966/967, 1055/1056, 1583/1598/1618, 1662/1664, 1676, 1842/1843 — the plain-paste path and its callees (`deleteSelection` 3859, `insertPlainText` 4271, `withUndoUnit` 3839) contain no reference, so the guard is not reached indirectly under another name. The keydown guard at 1056 only blocks a Cmd+Shift+V that starts while a paste is pending; in the reported ordering the plain read starts first, then `handlePaste`→`runPaste` sets `pasting = true` (1598) and `deferPaste` yields via `yieldToPaintedFrame()` (1603-1621), leaving a gap in which the resolved plain-text promise writes against the caret the in-flight paste owns. The mechanism is live in production: the host installs `largePasteHandler` at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:501 through `editor.onLargePaste` (editor.ts:4289), so `runPaste` really does defer for payloads over LARGE_PASTE_WEIGHT_THRESHOLD (text-editor.ts:50). The closest analogue reinforces the finding rather than refuting it: the other async-clipboard entry point, `EditorAPI.paste()` (editor.ts:3905-3937), routes its post-await write through `pasteContent`, which does check `if (this.pasting) return` (1664) precisely because a pending paste would interleave and its `finally` would clear the flag early. No counterexample found; the narrow timing window is a severity/confidence consideration, not a refutation ground.

finding.summary: Toolbar multi-block actions (`toggleList`, `indent`, `outdent`, `applyBlockStyle`, cell-range styling) still write once per block with no `batch()`, so they keep the exact #1045 failure the change fixes for the keyboard paths: on a select-all they exceed Yorkie's 50-entry undo cap and become partly un-undoable.
finding.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3356` (`applyBlockStyle`), `:3517` (`toggleList`), `:3539` (`indent`), `:3562` (`outdent`) and `:4149` (cell-range style loop) all do `docStore.snapshot(); forEachBlockInSelection(block => doc.setBlockType/applyBlockStyle(...))` with no `doc.batch(...)`. Each inner write is its own `YorkieDocStore.withUpdate` → `doc.update()` → one `doc.history` entry, so select-all + "Bulleted list" on a 100-paragraph document costs ~100 entries against `MaxUndoRedoStackDepth = 50`; `pushUndo` shifts the oldest off and the first ~50 blocks can never be restored. This is the same shape the diff documents as fixed "since issue #1045" (`docs/design/docs/docs-collaboration.md:305-311` claims "every selection-replacing edit" / "All editing paths"), but these paths never call `TextEditor.withUndoUnit` (they are `EditorAPI` methods, not `TextEditor` handlers). Fix belongs at these call sites: wrap the loop in `doc.batch(...)` (snapshot outside, as `withUndoUnit` requires).

verdict.reason: The absence itself checks out — editor.ts:3356/3517/3539/3562/4149 do run per-block `doc.applyBlockStyle`/`setBlockType`/`applyCellStyle` with only `docStore.snapshot()` and no `doc.batch()`, and yorkie-doc-store.ts:2951 (snapshot = no-op) plus :2899-2907 (a fresh `doc.update()` per write outside a batch) confirm each write is its own `doc.history` entry against the 50-entry cap at :574-587. What does not check out is the blocking rationale. The reviewer says the change documents these paths as fixed ("All editing paths"); the change documents the exact opposite, naming these very paths: docs-collaboration.md:313-321 "**Not yet every multi-write action.** `withUndoUnit()` is a `TextEditor` method, so it covers the keyboard and clipboard handlers and nothing else. The `EditorAPI` toolbar operations that write once per block — `toggleList` / `indent` / `outdent` / `applyBlockStyle` and the cell-range style loop — and `FindReplaceState.replaceAll()` still issue an unbatched write per block … Tracked in issue #1048". The line 309 sentence is about routing writes through `withUpdate` rather than `doc.update` (so a nested update cannot split an open batch), not about batch coverage. Under this lens's rubric that puts the finding out of lane: these EditorAPI methods never routed through `TextEditor.withUndoUnit`, do not reach it now, depend on no contract the change altered, and behave identically to before it ("still issue", "exactly as the keyboard paths did before #1045") — so there is no new guard being bypassed and no site the change leaves broken. It is a pre-existing, in-tree-documented, ticket-owned gap; the doc-scope aspect is design-fit's call, which already graded it minor.

finding.summary: `FindReplaceState.replaceAll()` performs two store writes per match with no `batch()`, so a large Replace All still overflows Yorkie's 50-entry undo cap and cannot be fully undone — the same bug class this change fixes elsewhere.
finding.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/find-replace.ts:69-87`: `replaceAll` calls `this.snapshot?.()` once and then `replaceMatch` per match, which issues `doc.deleteText(...)` + `doc.insertText(...)` — two separate `YorkieDocStore` writes, i.e. two `doc.update()`s and two undo entries per match. The host wires it to the real store (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-find-bar.tsx:67` passes `() => editor.getStore().snapshot()`; `:145` calls `state.replaceAll(replacement)`), so replacing >25 occurrences pushes past the 50-entry cap and the oldest replacements become permanently un-undoable. Nothing in the diff routes this path through `withUndoUnit`/`Doc.batch`. Fix belongs here: wrap the loop in `this.doc.batch(...)` with the snapshot outside it.

verdict.reason: The factual absence is real — I confirmed `FindReplaceState.replaceAll()` (packages/docs/src/view/find-replace.ts:69-87) loops `replaceMatch`, issuing separate `doc.deleteText` + `doc.insertText` per match with no `batch()`, that `docs-find-bar.tsx:141-148` calls it unwrapped (no `.batch(` anywhere under packages/frontend/src/app/docs/), that each store write opens its own `doc.update` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1714, :1809, :2899-2907), that `snapshot()` is a no-op (:2951), and that the 50-entry Yorkie cap is real (:579-586). I found no counterexample. I refute on lane, not on facts. The repository's own contract doc, docs/design/docs/docs-collaboration.md:313-321, scopes the batch rollout explicitly: "`withUndoUnit()` is a `TextEditor` method, so it covers the keyboard and clipboard handlers and nothing else … and `FindReplaceState.replaceAll()` still issue an unbatched write per block (per *match*, twice, for Replace All) … Tracked in issue #1048; the fix is the same `doc.batch(...)` with the snapshot outside it." So the "one user action = one undo unit" invariant is documented as not covering this path — no module reads an invariant this site violates. Nothing in the change alters `replaceAll`'s behaviour, no caller of it is broken, no contract it depends on changed, and `batch()` is a grouping seam rather than a guard (packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:105), so there is no guard to bypass. This is an analogous latent bug at an untouched site that the diff's fix was deliberately not extended to — a tracked correctness/backlog item, outside the blast-radius lane's rubric (guard bypass, broken caller, changed contract, removed export, violated invariant, new required field).
